findings_en: The image displays a chest X-ray with no significant abnormalities. The lungs appear to be clear and healthy, without any visible opacities or consolidations. There is also no evidence of pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or cardiomegaly in the image. The diaphragm, heart, and other anatomical structures are also not visible in this particular image. Overall, the X-ray does not reveal any acute findings related to the lungs or the cardiovascular system.
rag_context:
=== RELEVANT GUIDELINES ===
- On PA chest X-ray, the RIGHT side appears on the LEFT of the image (patient facing you). Right lung has three lobes (upper, middle, lower); left lung has two lobes (upper, lower) with lingula. Always verify with cardiac apex (points left) and gastric bubble (left lower).
- Interstitial pneumonia presents with reticular or ground-glass opacities, predominantly in lower lobes. Linear opacities and septal thickening may be present. Often viral etiology (influenza, COVID-19, RSV).
